ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Gene regulation controls which proteins a cell makes, when and how much. Errors can cause developmental disorders, cancers, and metabolic disease, making it a key clinical concept.

sections.p: Genes are DNA sequences that encode proteins. Regulation ensures cells produce the right proteins at the right time, allowing specialization and response to environment.
b: Regulation occurs at transcription, RNA processing, translation, and protein stability

sections.p: Transcription factors bind promoter or enhancer regions, recruiting RNA polymerase. Epigenetic marks (DNA methylation, histone acetylation) open or close chromatin, influencing access.
b: Promoter: core binding site near transcription start
GC box (-100 to -150) recruits Sp1 factor
Operon model explains coordinated bacterial gene control

sections.p: Multiple layers fine‑tune expression: transcription factors, co‑activators/repressors, chromatin remodelers, non‑coding RNAs, and feedback loops.
b: Epigenetic changes can be reversible or heritable

sections.p: Mutations in regulatory regions, abnormal transcription factor activity, or epigenetic dys‑regulation can lead to disease.
b: Promoter mutations → loss of tumor suppressor expression
Defective operon regulation causes bacterial resistance

sections.p: Understanding gene regulation guides diagnosis (e.g., methylation panels), therapy (epigenetic drugs), and prognosis in cancers, congenital disorders, and metabolic disease.
b: Methylation-specific PCR detects silenced tumor suppressors
HDAC inhibitors reactivate suppressed genes in lymphoma
Gene‑editing targets regulatory elements for therapy

sections.p: Focus on how regulatory defects produce clinical phenotypes and which tests reveal them.

t.b: Does the tumor have promoter hypermethylation? Hypermethylation suggests epigenetic silencing of tumor suppressor genes.

faq.q: Why does folate deficiency affect gene regulation?
faq.a: Folate provides methyl groups for DNA methylation; deficiency can lead to hypomethylation and abnormal gene expression.

faq.q: What is the difference between a promoter and an enhancer?
faq.a: Promoters sit immediately upstream of the transcription start site; enhancers can be distant and loop to influence transcription.

faq.q: Can gene regulation be targeted therapeutically?
faq.a: Yes, drugs like HDAC inhibitors or DNA‑methyltransferase inhibitors modify epigenetic marks to restore normal expression.

exam: Explain how promoter hypermethylation can silence a tumor suppressor gene and how this is detected.
